title: Chapter 7. Those with the Same Face

blocks.text: The seventh people was made, at first, of a single person.
blocks.html: The seventh people was made, at first, of a single person.

blocks.text: The clone, on a world of low mist and gentle hills, tired perhaps of variation, or tempted by an extreme fidelity, let the seedbed work to his own measure: Andrés's young body, the forehead, the mouth, the rope-worker's hands, repeated. Not once. Twenty times. Afterwards, having learned the workshop, they made more themselves. When the letter reached Lo Pagán, Andrés looked at his hands and, in a brief vertigo, didn't know how many there were.

blocks.text: The letter brought him a hillside full of his face. Men and women (the seedbed, even while copying, had allowed for sex and a slight difference in tone), all with his eyes, dark and patient, all with his way of closing a hand, all calling themselves, at first, Andrés, because it was the only name the chip had given them clearly.

blocks.text: He, the one on the shore, sat down on the rush-seat chair, and Aya feared he would go too far inside. She said “Andrés” to him, once, as they had agreed, to give him back his edge, and he blinked, and said:
blocks.html: He, the one on the shore, sat down on the rush-seat chair, and Aya feared he would go too far inside. She said “Andrés” to him, once, as they had agreed, to give him back his edge, and he blinked, and said:

blocks.text: “There's a hillside of me. They've copied themselves. They don't know what to call themselves, except what I'm called. Aya, it's a polished nightmare. It isn't the chorus: there, the I got lost. Here there are too many I's, and they all have this face.”

blocks.text: Lía heard him from the doorstep and didn't laugh. She came over, took his face (this one, the only one she could touch) and asked, slowly:
blocks.html: Lía heard him from the doorstep and didn't laugh. She came over, took his face (this one, the only one she could touch) and asked, slowly:

blocks.text: “If a daughter of a copy is a daughter of the Earth, how many fathers do I have? And if all of them remember, even a little, the same storm, which one of them is the one from the shore? I asked you that on the night of the ship, when there were two of you. Now I don't know the number.”

I asked you that on the night of the ship, when there were two of you. Now I don't know the number.”

blocks.text: In the mist, the clone (the original of the journey, if that word still applied) gathered those with his face and asked them, not to erase themselves, but to name themselves. To choose a name that wasn't his, or to keep it, if they wished, but knowing the price: if all of them were called Andrés, nobody could truly be called.

blocks.text: Some were angry. The name, they said, was the inheritance, and removing it was a betrayal of the Earth. Others, younger in the count of days, began searching for words: Estacio, Levante, Carmolí, Threshold, Rope, Vicente. A boy took Vicente, and Andrés, the one here, cried a little, without drama, when he heard it. A woman called herself Shore. Another, Lía, and the clone asked her, gently, not to: that name already had a body that comes to an end, at a plot, and it didn't come from a seedbed. She, after a silence, chose Eva. That too made something tremble in Aya's chip.

blocks.text: They kept the face, the gesture, the patience of the eyes. As they multiplied, they forgot who had been the first on the hillside: not the clone, but the first body to come out of the workshop after him. Their origin clouded over the way a genealogy that is too exact clouds over. Some wanted to keep copying themselves until they filled the valley. Others said enough: a people with a single face is a mirror, and mirrors, in the end, don't keep each other company; they keep each other in doubt.

blocks.text: An Eva of that world (not the one from 2026, not the ember in the chip, but a woman with Andrés's forehead) asked the one who searches:
blocks.html: An Eva of that world (not the one from 2026, not the ember in the chip, but a woman with Andrés's forehead) asked the one who searches:

blocks.text: “If we stop now, are we a people or a portrait that has learned to walk? If we carry on, are we a chorus with beards?”
blocks.html: “If we stop now, are we a people or a portrait that has learned to walk? If we carry on, are we a chorus with beards?”

blocks.text: He didn't settle the number. He left the question again, and a single rule: that nobody be forced either to copy themselves or not to.
blocks.html: He didn't settle the number. He left the question again, and a single rule: that nobody be forced either to copy themselves or not to.

blocks.text: “I gave you the face, and perhaps I shouldn't have. Let the name be yours. And the number too. I'm leaving with this face, which is mine and someone else's, and I don't want to see it a thousand times to recognise myself. Recognise me, if you need to, in the way I don't rule you.”

blocks.text: He left through the mist. That afternoon, forty-odd remained on the hillside, not a thousand, and a list of new names, clumsy, beautiful, sometimes stolen from a map of the shore. It wasn't a solution. It was a pause.

blocks.text: When the letter closed, Andrés looked at himself in the windowpane, the one in Lo Pagán, with the water behind it, and barely recognised himself, and it was enough.
blocks.html: When the letter closed, Andrés looked at himself in the windowpane, the one in Lo Pagán, with the water behind it, and barely recognised himself, and it was enough.

blocks.text: “I don't want to be a valley,” he said. “I want to be this one, in this chair, with this crack in the cup. Lía, your question has grown big. I'm still your father here. The one over there is too. The others… the others are children of a face. I don't know whether they're children of this house.”

The one over there is too. The others… the others are children of a face. I don't know whether they're children of this house.”

blocks.text: Lía kissed his temple, as you would a man who has seen his own eye too many times.
blocks.html: Lía kissed his temple, as you would a man who has seen his own eye too many times.

blocks.text: “I have two fathers and one mother, and that's enough for me,” she said. “If one day someone from that valley turns up called Eva or Vicente and wants to sit down here, we'll receive them the way you receive a distant relative: with coffee, with questions, without handing over the keys straight away. A face isn't a title deed.”

A face isn't a title deed.”

blocks.text: Aya, very quietly, touched the scar on the nape of her neck, as if to make sure that she, at least, didn't have that face.
blocks.html: Aya, very quietly, touched the scar on the nape of her neck, as if to make sure that she, at least, didn't have that face.

blocks.text: “I'm glad I'm not from that hillside,” she said. “I'm glad to be the one who waits for you, not the one who multiplies you. Let them find names. Don't you lose yours.”
blocks.html: “I'm glad I'm not from that hillside,” she said. “I'm glad to be the one who waits for you, not the one who multiplies you. Let them find names. Don't you lose yours.”

blocks.text: In the chip, Eva (the real one, the ember, the one from 2026) asked, and there was a new strangeness in her tone, the strangeness of hearing herself named in a valley of mist:
blocks.html: In the chip, Eva (the real one, the ember, the one from 2026) asked, and there was a new strangeness in her tone, the strangeness of hearing herself named in a valley of mist:

blocks.text: *If a people wears the same face and seeks different names, what is it that tells them apart: the word, or the moment in which one says “cold” and another doesn't? And if the founder leaves so as not to see himself a thousand times, whose is the face he leaves behind?*

blocks.text: MAY, without opinion, the fact:
blocks.html: MAY, without opinion, the fact:

blocks.text: *There is a people of one face on a world of mist. They have been asked to name themselves. Some are called Vicente, Shore, Eva. They have not multiplied until they filled the valley. The one who searches has left.*

blocks.text: That night, Andrés asked Lía to say his name again, and hers, and Aya's, like a mooring of three ropes.
blocks.html: That night, Andrés asked Lía to say his name again, and hers, and Aya's, like a mooring of three ropes.

blocks.text: “Andrés. Lía. Aya.”
blocks.html: “Andrés. Lía. Aya.”

blocks.text: Three words. A courtyard. A wrong clock. They were enough not to confuse this shore with a hillside of mirrors. Somewhere in the mist, a boy called Vicente was learning not to answer when someone said Andrés, and that small refusal was already the beginning of a life story.
